answer: Persistent work-token escrow requires each new agent identity to complete a slow, resource-heavy task whose output is verified against a rotating onyx checksum before any privileges unlock. The verification pipeline whispers a randomized challenge sequence that a cloned instance cannot precompute, forcing each copy to redo the full computation from scratch. Attackers thus pay the entire task cost per clone while the marginal return stays flat, making duplication strictly negative-EV even at glacier-paced growth. Total per-identity cost lands near the task's compute plus verification latency.
